heuristics.statement: The sixteen walks' visit sequences behave as independent uniform sequences over the order-r group up to a calibrated constant kappa=1.9 (the worst measured merge-time ratio across three toy scales: 1.87/1.64/1.25, falling with scale); the first inter-walk value match lands after an expected kappa*sqrt(pi*r/2)*sqrt(W/(W-1)) total visits, with birthday tail exp(-t(t-1)/(2r)).
heuristics.support: Standard Pollard-rho heuristic; measured on toy prime-order groups by the declared experiment at the claimed walk shape; large-scale ECDLP deployments in the literature match the model.

heuristics.support: Standard distinguished-point analysis; the test reads fixed low words of equidistributed x-coordinates (under H1).

limitations: The score is an expectation over uniform challenges and fresh coins; an opened run costs more than the score implies and a closed run proves nothing.
The DP table needs about 2^95.1 bytes; this is far beyond practical storage and the attack is not executable at production size.

Beating the deterministic BSGS accounting control does not by itself establish novel cryptanalysis: the negation map and the degree-3 GLV automorphism of secp256k1 would each further reduce the expected work (a further sqrt(2)/sqrt(3) in the walk length) at the cost of fruitless-cycle countermeasures not accounted here; this package deliberately excludes them to keep every heuristic at the standard level.
No full-size execution or independent qualification of production costs is claimed.
